mainTopic: The שתי הלחם of שבועות: how they are tied to the two lambs, and why loaves brought without lambs are left to spoil before burning
overview: This amud is about the שתי הלחם, the two loaves brought on שבועות. It opens by finishing a question about whether waving (תנופה) ties the loaves to the two lambs. It then asks a follow-up: if waving creates no bond, do replacement loaves need their own waving? That follow-up is narrowed to רבי עקיבא's view and ends in תיקו. Next, אביי asks רבא why only the two lambs sanctify the bread, and not the other שבועות offerings. The shared waving and the comparison to a תודה are both rejected. The גמרא settles on the איל נזיר: among several offerings, only the שלמים sanctifies the bread, as a ברייתא learns from a פסוק. Finally, a ברייתא says that loaves brought without lambs are waved, left until they spoil, and then burned. To explain why they wait, רבה says they are fit to eat but forbidden by a גזירה, and he brings a proof from the משנה in שקלים. אביי and רב יוסף push this aside. רבא agrees with רבה's ruling but proves it from a פסוק that compares the loaves to בכורים.

steps.title: If waving creates a bond, losing one side loses the other
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the first side of the question about תנופה. If waving creates a זיקה, then losing the bread loses the lambs, and losing the lambs loses the bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If the bread was lost,] the lambs are lost too. If the lambs were lost, the bread is lost too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the first possibility of the question: if waving ties the loaves and lambs together, losing either one means the whole set is lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the waving joins the two loaves and the two lambs into one unit. So if one half disappears after the waving, the other half cannot be used with a new partner. You must start over with both loaves and lambs.

keyTerms.meaning: A bond or link that ties two things together legally
Lambs; here, the two lambs brought with the שתי הלחם on שבועות
The bread; here, the שתי הלחם (two loaves) of שבועות
They were lost (or became unusable)

phrases.english: the lambs are lost;
if the lambs were lost, the bread is lost.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָבְדוּ כְּבָשִׂים, אָבְדוּ כְּבָשִׂים – אָבַד הַלֶּחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first side of רבי ירמיה's question (תנופה עושה זיקה), which began before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether waving creates a binding link between the loaves and the lambs, so that losing one disqualifies the other.

steps.title: Follow-up: do replacement loaves need waving?
steps.stepSummary: Suppose waving does NOT create a bond. After the waving the bread was lost and new bread was brought. Does the new bread need its own waving?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you conclude that waving does not create a bond: someone brought bread and lambs, and they were waved. Then the bread was lost and he brought other bread. Does that bread need waving or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a second question on top of the first one. It only works if the answer to the first question is that waving creates no bond.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is no bond, the lambs can stay and new loaves can take the place of the lost ones. But the new loaves were never waved. Does the waving already done with the lambs count, or must the new loaves be waved again?

keyTerms.meaning: If you conclude that... (it opens a follow-up question that assumes one answer to the first question)
Waving; the required waving of the offering
They were waved
Requires, needs

steps.confusionAlert: This question does NOT decide whether waving creates a bond. It only asks what happens if the answer turns out to be 'no bond'. The first question is still open.

phrases.english: And if you conclude that
waving does not create a bond,
if he brought bread and lambs and they were waved,
and the bread was lost, and he brought other bread,
does that bread require waving,
or does it not require waving?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the 'no bond' side of the question in Step 1 and asks a new question built on it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether replacement loaves need their own waving when the original set was already waved with the lambs.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a 'no bond' answer does not settle everything. We still have to know whether the waving belongs to the lambs or to the bread.

steps.title: The question only applies when the bread was lost
steps.stepSummary: If the lambs were lost, the new lambs surely need waving, so there is no question. The question is only when the bread was lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the lambs were lost, you should not ask, because they certainly need waving. When should you ask? When the bread was lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the follow-up question. It points out that one case is obvious, so the real question is only about the other case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New lambs plainly need waving. That is why losing the lambs is no question. The open case is new bread joining lambs that were already waved: maybe the earlier waving of the lambs is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't ask this; this case is obvious
When you should ask is... (it points to the real case in doubt)
Certainly, definitely
Needs, requires

phrases.english: If the lambs were lost, do not ask,
for they certainly require waving;
phrases.notes: 'They' means the new lambs brought in place of the lost ones.

phrases.english: when should you ask? When the bread was lost.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ, כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from Step 2 to the case where the bread, not the lambs, was lost.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Replacement lambs definitely need waving; the doubt is only about replacement bread.

steps.title: The question only applies according to רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: According to בן ננס, the lambs are the main part, so there is no question. The question is only according to רבי עקיבא, who holds the bread is the main part. So what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to בן ננס you should not ask, since he says the lambs are the main part. When should you ask? According to רבי עקיבא, who says the bread is the main part. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the question one more time. It applies only according to one opinion, and then asks it plainly: what is the law?
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן ננס holds the lambs are the main part, so the lambs were already waved and that is enough. רבי עקיבא holds the bread is the main part, so maybe new bread needs its own waving. Step 5 lays out both sides, and step 6 ends with תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: According to (someone's opinion)
The main, essential part
What? (what is the law?)

steps.whatToRemember: The final, narrow question has three parts. Waving creates no bond. The bread was lost after the waving. The question follows רבי עקיבא, who holds the bread is the main part. Does the new bread need its own waving?

phrases.aramaic: וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּבֶן נַנָּס, לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ,
phrases.english: And according to Ben Nannas, do not ask,
for he says the lambs are primary.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: When should you ask? According to Rabbi Akiva,
who says the bread is primary — what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּבֶן נַנָּס, לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from Steps 2 and 3 to רבי עקיבא's opinion and asks it directly.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי עקיבא (bread is the main part), do replacement loaves need waving when the lambs were already waved with the lost loaves?
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the waving question to the argument over which part of the offering is the main one. Who is 'primary' decides whose waving counts.

steps.title: Two sides: does the new bread need waving?
steps.stepSummary: From רבי עקיבא's view, the גמרא gives two ways to look at the replacement bread. Because the bread is the main part, maybe it needs its own תנופה. Or, because the lambs are what permit it and they were already waved, maybe it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the bread is the main part, does it need waving? Or perhaps, since the things that permit it are the lambs, it does not need waving?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two sides of the question it just asked about the replacement bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one says the bread is the main part, and this new bread was never waved, so it should need its own waving. Side two says the bread only becomes permitted through the lambs, and the lambs were already waved, so that waving is enough. Each side looks at a different relationship between the bread and the lambs.

keyTerms.meaning: The main or central part
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
The things that permit an offering, such as the blood of the animals
Waving of an offering

phrases.english: Since the bread is the main part,
it needs waving,
phrases.notes: The new bread was never waved, so maybe it needs its own waving.

phrases.english: or perhaps, since its permitting factors
are the lambs,
phrases.notes: The lambs were already waved, so their waving might cover the bread too.

phrases.english: it does not need waving.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּלֶחֶם עִיקָּר בָּעֵי תְּנוּפָה אוֹ דִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the two sides of the question stated in step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a replacement set of loaves need its own תנופה, according to רבי עקיבא?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: the question is left without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot decide between the two sides, so it leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether the new bread needs waving. תיקו means the question simply stands, and this closes the section about תנופה and replacement offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Whether replacement bread needs its own תנופה, according to רבי עקיבא, is left as a תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from step 5 without a resolution

steps.title: Why only the two lambs are tied to the bread
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבא why the two lambs of שבועות sanctify the bread and hold it back, while the seven lambs, bull and rams brought that day do neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבא: What is different about the two lambs, which sanctify the bread and hold it back, and what is different about the seven lambs, the bull and the rams, which do not sanctify the bread and do not hold it back?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. אביי asks why only the two שלמים lambs have a legal link to the שבועות bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many animals are brought on שבועות, but only the two lambs sanctify the loaves when they are slaughtered. Only they hold back the bread if they are not brought. אביי wants the reason for this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asks for the reason behind two different rulings
They sanctify (the bread becomes fully holy through their slaughter)
They hold back: without them, the other offering cannot be brought
The extra (מוסף) offerings of שבועות

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rava:
What is different about the two lambs,
that they sanctify the bread and hold it back,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי שְׁנָא שִׁבְעָה כְּבָשִׂים וּפַר וְאֵילִים
phrases.english: and what is different about the seven lambs, the bull and the rams,
that they do not sanctify the bread and do not hold it back?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרָבָא מַאי שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the תיקו
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why do the two שלמים lambs sanctify and hold back the bread, but the מוסף animals do not?

steps.title: רבא: because they are waved together
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the two lambs and the bread are bound together through their shared תנופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because they are bound to each other through the waving.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his first answer: the shared waving is what links the lambs to the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two lambs and the loaves are waved together, but the מוסף animals are not waved with the bread. So רבא says the shared תנופה creates the link that makes the lambs sanctify the bread and hold it back.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
They became bound to one another

phrases.english: He said to him: Because they are bound
to each other through the waving.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הוֹאִיל וְהוּזְקְקוּ זֶה לָזֶה בִּתְנוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shared תנופה binds the two lambs to the bread.

steps.title: Challenge from the thanks offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: a תודה and its loaves are not waved together, yet the תודה still sanctifies the loaves and holds them back.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a thanks offering is not bound to its loaves through waving, and yet it sanctifies them and holds them back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's answer by pointing to the תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If shared waving were the reason, then a תודה, which is not waved together with its bread, should not sanctify or hold back its loaves. But it does both. So waving cannot be the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: But look at (introduces a counter-example)
Thanks offering, brought together with loaves

phrases.english: But there is the thanks offering,
where they are not bound to each other through waving,
and yet it sanctifies and holds back!
phrases.notes: The slaughter of the תודה sanctifies its loaves, and the loaves can't be brought without it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי תּוֹדָה דְּלֹא הוּזְקְקוּ זֶה לָזֶה בִּתְנוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the shared תנופה is the reason
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תודה has the same law with no shared waving, so waving cannot be the cause.

steps.title: The lambs are שלמים, like a תודה
steps.stepSummary: The new reason: the two lambs are like a תודה. A תודה is a type of שלמים, and the two lambs are also שלמים, so they share its law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like a thanks offering: just as a thanks offering is a peace offering, so too here it is a peace offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the waving reason and gives a new one: the lambs are שלמים, just like a תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case that broke רבא's answer now becomes the model for the new answer. A תודה is a שלמים and sanctifies and holds back its bread. The two lambs are also שלמים, so they do the same. The seven lambs, the bull and the rams in אביי's question are עולות, not שלמים, so they do not.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer and gives a new one)
Peace offerings
Like a thanks offering, a comparison to the תודה

steps.whatToRemember: The waving answer was dropped. The new idea is that the two lambs are שלמים, like a תודה. The next step shows this comparison is not enough by itself, and step 12 replaces it with the איל נזיר.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the waving explains the link; the גמרא rejected that idea. The תודה comparison is not the final answer either. The גמרא ends up with the איל נזיר in step 12.

phrases.english: Rather, it is like a thanks offering:
just as a thanks offering is a peace offering,
so too here it is also a peace offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כְּתוֹדָה מָה תּוֹדָה שְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by replacing רבא's reason with a new one
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the reason with a comparison to תודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The shared תנופה binds the lambs and the bread.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lambs are שלמים like a תודה, so they sanctify the bread and hold it back.

steps.title: The תודה comparison does not fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison to a תודה. A תודה is brought alone, but on שבועות many other offerings come with the lambs, so why shouldn't they all sanctify the bread?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this really the same? There, by a תודה, no other offerings come with it. Here, on שבועות, other offerings do come with it, so let all of them sanctify the bread!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 10, which compared the two lambs to a תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה sanctifies its loaves, but it is the only animal there, so there is nothing to choose between. On שבועות there are many other animals besides the lambs. The תודה case cannot tell us why the lambs alone sanctify the bread and the other offerings do not.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they really alike? This opens a challenge to a comparison
Other animal offerings
Together with it
These and those, meaning both groups

phrases.english: Are they comparable?
There, there are no other offerings with it,
phrases.notes: "There" is the תודה, which is brought with no other animals.

phrases.english: but here, where there are other offerings with it,
let these and those sanctify the bread!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the תודה comparison offered in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of the two lambs of שבועות to a תודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תודה has no other offerings beside it, so it cannot explain why, out of many offerings on שבועות, only the שלמים lambs sanctify the bread.

steps.title: The lambs are like the איל נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a better comparison: the איל נזיר. A נזיר brings other offerings too, yet only his שלמים ram sanctifies his loaves. The same is true on שבועות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like the ram of a נזיר. Just as with the ram of a נזיר, even though other offerings come with it, only the שלמים sanctifies the bread and nothing else does, here too it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new model that fits better: the offerings a נזיר brings when his נזירות ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר brings a עולה, a חטאת and a שלמים ram together, plus a basket of loaves. Only the שלמים ram sanctifies the loaves. This matches שבועות exactly: many offerings are brought, but only the שלמים lambs sanctify the bread.

keyTerms.meaning: The ram a נזיר brings as a שלמים when his נזירות ends
Peace offerings
They sanctify
It is no different

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule: when bread comes along with a group of offerings, it is the שלמים that sanctifies it, not the other offerings.

phrases.english: Rather, it is like the ram of a נזיר.
Just as with the ram of a נזיר,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא זְבָחִים אַחֲרִינִי,
phrases.english: even though there are other offerings with it,
phrases.notes: The נזיר also brings a עולה and a חטאת at the same time.

phrases.english: it is the שלמים that sanctifies the bread,
and nothing else does,
here too it is no different.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כְּאֵיל נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected תודה comparison with the איל נזיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New comparison that matches the case better
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lambs are like a תודה, which sanctifies its loaves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lambs are like the איל נזיר: among several offerings, only the שלמים sanctifies the bread.

steps.title: Where do we learn this about the נזיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that only the נזיר's שלמים ram sanctifies his loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, by the נזיר, how do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just built on the נזיר case, so now it asks how we know the rule there in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from step 12 only works if the נזיר rule is solid. So the גמרא asks for its source before relying on it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And there, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: "There" means the נזיר: how do we know only his שלמים ram sanctifies the loaves?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתָם מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the נזיר rule used in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that only the איל נזיר, the שלמים, sanctifies the נזיר's loaves.

steps.title: The פסוק links the basket to the ram
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that the basket of loaves belongs to the ram, and the ram's שחיטה sanctifies them. So if the ram was slaughtered for the wrong purpose, the bread is not sanctified.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: "And he shall make the ram a שלמים offering to ה' with the basket of מצות." This teaches that the basket comes as an obligation for the ram, and the ram's שחיטה sanctifies the loaves. Therefore, if he slaughtered it not for its own sake, the bread is not sanctified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that reads the פסוק as tying the loaves to the ram.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places the basket "with" the ram, the שלמים, and not with the other offerings. So the ram's שחיטה is what makes the bread holy. The proof of this: if the ram's שחיטה is spoiled by being done for a different purpose, the bread does not become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: The basket of מצה loaves a נזיר brings
An obligation that belongs to the ram, meaning the bread comes because of the ram
Slaughtering the animal
Not for its own sake, meaning slaughtered as a different kind of offering

steps.whatToRemember: The bread follows the שלמים: its שחיטה sanctifies the bread, and if that שחיטה is done for the wrong purpose, the bread is not sanctified.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"And he shall make the ram a שלמים offering
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:17

phrases.english: to ה', with the basket of מצות";
this teaches that the basket comes as an obligation for the ram,
and the slaughtering of the ram sanctifies them.
Therefore, if he slaughtered it not for its own sake,
the bread did not become sanctified.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: וְאֶת הָאַיִל יַעֲשֶׂה זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים לַה׳ עַל סַל הַמַּצּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 with a ברייתא based on a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק joins the basket to the שלמים ram, so the ram's שחיטה alone sanctifies the loaves; if done not for its own sake, the bread is not sanctified.

steps.title: שתי הלחם brought without the lambs
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: if the שתי הלחם are brought without the lambs, they are waved, left until they spoil, and then taken out to be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The שתי הלחם that are brought by themselves are waved, left until their form spoils, and then taken out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about the case where the bread is brought without any lambs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without lambs, the usual thing that permits the bread is missing. The ברייתא says the bread still gets a תנופה, then waits until it spoils, and only then is burned like other disqualified offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות
By themselves, without the lambs
They are waved, given תנופה
Their form passes, meaning they are left overnight until they become unfit
The place where unfit offerings are burned

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the bread ends up burned, it is still waved first. The waving does not depend on having the lambs.

phrases.english: The רבנן taught:
The two loaves that are brought by themselves
phrases.notes: "By themselves" means with no lambs brought along with them.

phrases.english: are waved, and their form is left to spoil,
and they go out to the place of burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם הַבָּאוֹת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section about the שתי הלחם brought without lambs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שתי הלחם brought without lambs are waved, left until they become unfit, and then burned.

steps.title: Why wait for the loaves to spoil?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: either the loaves are meant to be eaten or meant to be burned, so why leave them to spoil first?
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it, there is a problem. If the loaves are brought to be eaten, let them be eaten. If they are brought to be burned, let them be burned right away. Why leave them until they spoil?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling from Step 15 that the שתי הלחם without lambs are left to spoil and only then burned. It says the middle path makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There seem to be only two options. Either the bread is fit to eat, so eat it, or it is not, so burn it now. Waiting for the bread to spoil (עיבור צורה) only makes sense if the bread is fit but still may not be eaten, and the גמרא does not yet see how that could be.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it. It sets up a two-sided challenge where both options fail.
Losing its form. The bread is left overnight until it becomes unfit, and only then is it burned.
Immediately, right away
Burning, here the burning of קדשים that may not be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking why the bread is burned in the end. It is asking why it must wait and spoil first instead of being burned right away.

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it, there is a problem:
If they are brought to be eaten, let them eat them;
if they are brought to be burned, let them burn them immediately.
Why do they need a decay of form?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה נַפְשָׁךְ? אִי לַאֲכִילָה אָתְיָין – לֵיכְלִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the ברייתא brought in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that שתי הלחם brought without the lambs are left to spoil and then burned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided dilemma: if the loaves are fit to eat they should be eaten, and if not they should be burned at once. Waiting fits neither option.

steps.title: רבה: the loaves are fit, but the חכמים decreed not to eat them
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that by Torah law the loaves may be eaten. The חכמים forbade them by a גזירה so that people won't later eat bread without lambs when lambs are available.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Really, the loaves are fit to be eaten. But there is a decree, out of fear that next year lambs will be available and people will say, 'Last year we ate the bread without lambs, so now we will too.' They won't realize that last year there were no lambs, so the bread permitted itself. Now that there are lambs, it is the lambs that permit the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge. He chooses the side that the loaves are 'for eating', but says the חכמים forbade eating them for a practical reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, when there are no lambs, the loaves become permitted on their own. But in a normal year the lambs are what permit the bread, and people might mix up the two situations. So the חכמים forbade eating the bread, and since it is still fit by Torah law, it may not be burned until it spoils on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually. It introduces the answer by choosing one side of the question.
A protective decree of the חכמים to keep people from a mistake
Last year
They permit themselves. With no lambs, the loaves become permitted on their own.

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why there is a middle path between eating and burning: something fit by Torah law but forbidden by the חכמים may not be destroyed right away, so it is left until it becomes unfit by itself.
steps.whatToRemember: The שתי הלחם without lambs are fit by Torah law. They are not eaten only because of a rabbinic גזירה, so they are left to spoil before they are burned.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Actually, they are brought to be eaten;
but it is a decree, lest there become available to them
lambs the following year,
and they will say: Last year, didn't we eat
the bread without lambs?
Now too, we will eat it.
But they will not know
that last year there were no lambs,
so they permitted themselves;
phrases.notes: 'They' here means the loaves themselves. With no lambs, nothing else was needed to permit them.

phrases.english: now that there are lambs,
it is the lambs that permit them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: לְעוֹלָם לַאֲכִילָה אָתְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מה נפשך challenge of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side of the dilemma (for eating) and adds a rabbinic גזירה that explains the waiting.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bread must be either eaten or burned right away; there is no reason to wait.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bread is fit by Torah law but forbidden by a גזירה, so it may not be burned until it spoils on its own.

steps.title: רבה begins his source: בן בוכרי's testimony about a כהן's שקל
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks where he learned his idea and starts quoting a משנה: בן בוכרי testified in יבנה that a כהן who gives the half-שקל is not a sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: From where do I say this? As we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה said, בן בוכרי testified in יבנה that any כהן who gives the שקל is not a sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה is setting up a proof for his idea. He quotes the beginning of a משנה, and the explanation of how it proves his point comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only have the opening of the source: a כהן who gives the half-שקל, even though he isn't required to, does nothing wrong. Steps 19-20 continue the משנה. Steps 21-23 show how it connects to the שתי הלחם and to רבה's point.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? A sage introduces the source for his own statement.
Testified, reported a tradition before the חכמים
Gives the yearly half-שקל to the מקדש
A sinner, someone doing something wrong

phrases.english: Rabba said: From where do I say this?
As we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: שקלים 1:4

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Ben Bukhri testified in Yavne:
Any priest who gives the shekel is not a sinner.
phrases.notes: Giving the שקל means the yearly half-שקל donation to the מקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבה brings a source to support the answer he gave in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's explanation of why the שתי הלחם without lambs are not eaten.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שקלים quoting בן בוכרי's testimony in יבנה about a כהן who gives the half-שקל; the proof itself continues in the next lines.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: a כהן who doesn't give the שקל is a sinner
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי rejects בן בוכרי's statement. A כהן who does not give the half-שקל is a sinner. Some כהנים, however, twist a פסוק to excuse themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said to him: Not so! Any כהן who does not give the שקל is a sinner. But the כהנים interpret this פסוק for their own benefit:
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's answer to בן בוכרי. He says כהנים are fully obligated to give the half-שקל, and he sets up the excuse some of them use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן בוכרי said a כהן who gives is 'not a sinner', which hints that he isn't required to give. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי turns this around: not giving is the sin. He then sets up the next line, which explains the כהנים' self-serving reading of a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives the half-שקל to the Temple fund
A sinner
Interpret for their own benefit, in a self-serving way

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is בן בוכרי, who gave the testimony in יבנה from the previous step.

phrases.english: Not so!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁאֵינוֹ שׁוֹקֵל – חוֹטֵא,
phrases.english: Rather, any kohen who does not give the shekel is a sinner,
but the kohanim interpret
this verse for their own benefit:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי: לֹא כִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה that רבה began quoting in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן is obligated to give the half-שקל, and one who doesn't is a sinner.

steps.title: The כהנים' excuse from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים quote the פסוק that a כהן's מנחה must be fully burned. They argue that if they paid, the communal offerings would partly belong to them and could not be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And every מנחה of a כהן shall be completely burned; it shall not be eaten." Since the עומר, the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים are ours, how could they be eaten?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה spells out the כהנים' excuse for not paying. If they paid, these offerings would be 'theirs', and a כהן's מנחה can never be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Communal offerings are bought with the half-שקל money. So paying would make the כהנים partners in the עומר, the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים. Their argument assumes these offerings are normally eaten, and that hidden assumption is exactly what רבה will use.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal offering brought by a כהן, which must be burned completely
Completely, entirely burned
The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות
The showbread placed on the Table every שבת

phrases.english: "And every meal offering of a kohen
shall be completely burned; it shall not be eaten."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:16

phrases.english: Since the omer and the two loaves
and the showbread are ours,
phrases.notes: They mean: if we paid the half-שקל, we'd own a share, since these offerings are bought with that money.

phrases.english: how could they be eaten?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל מִנְחַת כֹּהֵן כָּלִיל תִּהְיֶה לֹא תֵאָכֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the self-serving reading that step 19 introduced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים assumed that the עומר, the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים are eaten, so being part-owners would make them forbidden as a כהן's מנחה.

steps.title: Which שתי הלחם does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks what case of שתי הלחם the משנה is talking about. He first suggests the loaves brought together with the lambs.
steps.simpleTranslation: These two loaves, what is the case? If you say it is when they come with the animal offering...
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the משנה has been quoted, the גמרא starts using it. It asks which situation the משנה's שתי הלחם refers to, and sets up a first possibility to test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible cases: loaves brought with the two lambs of שבועות, or loaves brought alone. Pinning down the case decides whether the משנה really supports רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What situation are we talking about?
If you say, which introduces a suggestion to be tested
Animal offering, here the two lambs of שבועות

phrases.english: These two loaves, what is the case?
If you say it is when they come with the animal offering,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבה begins analyzing the משנה he quoted, to draw his proof from it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's שתי הלחם are loaves brought with the lambs or loaves brought alone.

steps.title: It can't mean loaves brought with the lambs
steps.stepSummary: Loaves brought with an animal offering are like the bread of a תודה. A כהן may bring a תודה and eat its bread, so the כהנים would have had nothing to worry about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that כהנים don't donate a תודה and its bread and eat them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion. If the loaves come with the lambs, they are like a תודה's bread, which a כהן can bring and eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread that goes along with an animal offering is not counted as a separate מנחת כהן. So the rule 'it shall not be eaten' would not apply to it. The כהנים' worry only makes sense for loaves that come on their own.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? Used to ask a question with an obvious answer
A thanks offering and the loaves that come with it
They donate, bring as a voluntary offering

phrases.english: Is that to say that a thanks offering and its bread,
kohanim don't donate them
and eat them?
phrases.notes: Of course they do. So bread that comes with an animal offering is not a problem for a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ תּוֹדָה וְלַחְמָהּ מִי לָא מְנַדְּבִי כֹּהֲנִים וְאָכְלִי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'with the lambs' option raised in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the משנה refers to שתי הלחם brought with the lambs.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A כהן may eat bread that accompanies an animal offering, as with a תודה. So the כהנים would have had no reason to worry.

steps.title: So loaves without lambs are meant to be eaten
steps.stepSummary: The משנה must be talking about שתי הלחם brought alone. The כהנים still assumed they are eaten. This proves that by Torah law such loaves are meant to be eaten, as רבה said.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it when they come by themselves? And it teaches: "How could they be eaten?" Apparently, they come to be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the משנה is talking about loaves brought without lambs. This completes רבה's proof that such loaves are meant to be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים' whole worry was that loaves brought alone could no longer be eaten if they owned a share. That worry assumes such loaves are normally eaten. This backs רבה's claim from step 17: by Torah law they may be eaten, and only a rabbinic decree forbids them.

keyTerms.meaning: By themselves, without the lambs
Apparently, from this we see
They come to be eaten

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's proof: the כהנים' excuse in the משנה assumes that שתי הלחם brought alone are eaten, so by Torah law they are eaten and only a decree makes them wait. The next step (אביי) pushes this proof aside.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains the odd ברייתא from steps 15-16. The loaves are left to spoil instead of being burned right away because they are really fit to be eaten, and only a rabbinic decree stops people from eating them.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it when they come by themselves?
And it teaches: "How could they be eaten?"
Apparently, they come to be eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו בְּבָאוֹת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the 'with the lambs' option rejected, the only remaining case gives רבה his proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's claim that, by Torah law, שתי הלחם brought without lambs may be eaten.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in which the כהנים ask 'how could they be eaten?' about שתי הלחם, which must refer to loaves brought alone.

steps.title: אביי: The loaves may come with the lambs, and they are called a מנחה
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבה's proof. The משנה can be about שתי הלחם brought with the lambs. The כהנים worried because שתי הלחם are called a מנחה, unlike the bread of a תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Actually, the משנה is about loaves that come with the animal offering. As for your question from a תודה and its bread: the bread of a תודה is not called a 'מנחה', but the שתי הלחם are called a 'מנחה', as the פסוק says, 'when you bring a new מנחה to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down רבה's proof by going back to the first suggestion. The משנה could be about loaves brought together with the lambs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה had said that loaves brought with an animal are like the bread of a תודה, which a כהן may eat. אביי answers that there is a difference. The Torah calls שתי הלחם a 'מנחה', and a כהן's מנחה must be fully burned. The bread of a תודה is never called a מנחה. So the כהנים had a real worry even about loaves brought with lambs, and the משנה proves nothing about loaves brought alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really — used to go back to an earlier suggestion
Loaves that come together with an animal offering
The loaves brought with a thanks offering
A meal offering; a כהן's מנחה must be completely burned

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the bread of a תודה is a different kind of food. The whole point is the NAME: only something the Torah calls a 'מנחה' falls under the rule that a כהן's מנחה is fully burned.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him (to Rabba):
Actually, it is about loaves that come with the animal offering,
and as for what bothers you from a thanks offering and its bread —
phrases.notes: This is רבה's challenge from step 22: a כהן may bring a תודה and still eat its bread.

phrases.english: the loaves of a thanks offering are not called a "meal offering,"
but the two loaves are called a "meal offering,"
as it says: "When you bring a new meal offering to ה׳."
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:26

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם בְּבָאוֹת עִם הַזֶּבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 23 by reviving the option that step 22 had pushed aside
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבה's proof that שתי הלחם brought alone are eaten
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison to the bread of a תודה fails, because only שתי הלחם are called 'מנחה'

steps.title: רב יוסף: Loaves brought alone really are for burning
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a different answer to רבה. He says loaves brought without lambs are meant to be burned. They are left until the next day only because קדשים may not be burned on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Actually, they come to be burned. The reason we do not burn them right away is that we do not burn holy items on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a second, separate way to reject רבה's proof. He says loaves brought alone are not eaten at all; they are burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaves are not burned right away but are left over until after the day. One might think this shows they are not really meant for burning. רב יוסף explains that the delay has a different cause: holy items may not be burned on יום טוב, and שבועות is a יום טוב. So the delay tells us nothing about whether the loaves are eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: They come to be burned
Holy, consecrated items
A festival day; here, שבועות
And this is the reason

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Actually, they come to be burned,
phrases.notes: He means the שתי הלחם brought without lambs.

phrases.english: and this is the reason we do not burn them right away —

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין שׂוֹרְפִין קָדָשִׁים בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: because we do not burn holy items on a festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם לִשְׂרֵיפָה אָתְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent rejection of רבה's view, parallel to אביי's in step 24
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבה's claim that loaves brought alone are eaten by Torah law
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The delay before burning comes from the rule against burning on יום טוב, not from the loaves being meant to be eaten

steps.title: אביי: Burning that is the מצוה may be done on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף. The ban on burning on יום טוב applies only to items that became disqualified. If burning is the loaves' actual מצוה, they should be burned on יום טוב, just like the bull and goat of יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is this comparable? There, burning is not their מצוה. Here, where burning is their מצוה, let them burn them, just as with the bull and the goat of יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's reason for the delay. He argues the rule about not burning on יום טוב does not fit this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually קדשים are meant to be eaten, and burning is just a way to get rid of them when they become unfit. That kind of burning waits until after יום טוב. But if loaves brought alone are MEANT to be burned, burning them is a מצוה, and such burning is allowed even on a holy day. The proof is the פר and שעיר of יום הכיפורים, which are burned on that day itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it comparable? — a challenge that the cases are different
This (burning) is their proper מצוה
Just like — brings a parallel case
The bull and goat of יום הכיפורים, which are burned that day

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Is it comparable?
There — burning is not their מצוה,
phrases.notes: "There" means regular קדשים that became unfit; they were supposed to be eaten.

phrases.english: here — where burning is their מצוה, let them burn them,

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַפַּר וְשָׂעִיר שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: just as with the bull and the goat of Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's explanation in step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reason that the loaves wait because there is no burning on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Burning that is the item's מצוה is allowed on a holy day, as with the פר and שעיר of יום הכיפורים, so the reason fails

steps.title: רב יוסף: A rabbinic decree, in case lambs show up later
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a new reason for delaying the burning. The Rabbis decreed to wait, because lambs might become available later in the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: It is a decree, in case lambs become available to them afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף drops his first reason and gives a new one for why the loaves are not burned right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since אביי showed that burning on יום טוב is not the problem, רב יוסף now says the waiting is a rabbinic גזירה. If lambs turn up later that day, the loaves could be brought with them and eaten. Burning them too fast would ruin that chance. The loaves are still basically 'for burning'; only the timing is delayed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather — drops the earlier answer and offers a new one
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
Lest they become available
Lambs (the animals brought with שתי הלחם)

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
It is a decree, in case there become available to them
lambs afterward.
phrases.notes: If lambs turn up, the loaves can be brought with them and then eaten, so we hold off on burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: גְּזֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reason אביי rejected in step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason replacing the rejected one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The delay was because קדשים are not burned on יום טוב
steps.terutzMaskana: The delay is a rabbinic decree, in case lambs become available later that day

steps.title: אביי: Once the time for offering passes, burn them
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges again. The decree makes sense only while there is still time to offer lambs. After that time passes, the loaves should be burned at once, not left until the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: That works for the whole time they could be offered. After that, let them burn them!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי accepts the logic of the גזירה but says it cannot explain the full delay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lambs can only be offered during the day's offering time. Once that time is over, no lambs could be brought, and the worry disappears. So the loaves should be burned right then, which is still on the same day. Yet the ברייתא implies they wait longer.

keyTerms.meaning: That works out well — granted, for part of the case
The time when they may be offered
After that

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
That works for the whole time they could be offered,
but after that, let them burn them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: תִּינַח כׇּל זְמַן הַקְרָבָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the גזירה given in step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's גזירה as an explanation for the long delay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the offering time has passed, lambs can no longer come, so the decree has no reason to keep the loaves waiting

steps.title: "Their form decays" means the time for offering has passed
steps.stepSummary: The answer reads the ברייתא's phrase 'until their form decays' differently. It means until the time for offering them has passed, not until the bread spoils overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'their form will decay' that the ברייתא teaches? The 'form' of their offering, meaning the time when they could be offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי by reinterpreting the wording of the ברייתא. The phrase about the loaves' 'form decaying' does not have to mean waiting until the next day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed 'תעובר צורתן' means the bread itself must sit until it goes stale overnight. The answer explains that 'צורתן' here means the 'form of their offering', the window of time when lambs could still be brought. Once that window passes, they are burned, which is exactly what אביי said should happen. רב יוסף's גזירה therefore stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Their form will pass — normally means left overnight until they become unfit
The 'form' of their offering, meaning the time they could be offered
That it teaches (in the ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to reject רבה. אביי says the משנה could be about loaves brought with lambs, which are still called a 'מנחה'. רב יוסף says loaves brought alone are really burned. They wait only because of a גזירה in case lambs come, and 'תעובר צורתן' means the offering time has passed.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'צורה' does not mean the bread's physical shape or staleness. It means the 'form' of the offering, the time window when the loaves could still be brought with lambs.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "their form will decay" that it teaches?
— The form of their offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״תְּעוּבַּר צוּרָתָן״ נָמֵי דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 28 by rereading the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'תעובר צורתן' means the loaves wait overnight until they spoil
steps.terutzMaskana: 'צורתן' means the time for offering them; once that passes they are burned, so the גזירה works

steps.title: רבא: the loaves are meant to be eaten, and the delay is a decree
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the loaves brought without lambs are eaten by Torah law. Leaving them overnight is a rabbinic decree based on רבה's concern. But the Torah-law source is a פסוק, not רבה's reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The loaves come to be eaten. The Rabbis made a decree because of רבה's concern. But we know they are eaten not from רבה's reasoning, but from a verse.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third response. He agrees with רבה that the loaves are for eating and that the delay is a decree, but he gets the Torah-law rule from a פסוק rather than from the משנה in שקלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא sides fully with רבה on the law: by Torah law the loaves are eaten, and the delay is a decree for רבה's reason, the fear that in a later year people will eat the bread without lambs. He does not rely on רבה's proof from the משנה in שקלים, which can be pushed aside as אביי did in step 24. Instead he promises a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: They come to be eaten. This is their Torah-law purpose.
A rabbinic decree, made as a protective measure.
But not from his reasoning. רבא rejects רבה's source.
From a פסוק in the Torah.

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not fully disagree with רבה. He agrees on the halacha (they are eaten) and on the reason for the decree. He only disputes where the Torah-law rule comes from.

phrases.english: Rava said: They come to be eaten,
phrases.notes: He means the two loaves of שבועות that were brought without the lambs.

phrases.english: and there is a decree because of Rabba's concern,
phrases.notes: This is רבה's worry that people might eat the loaves without sheep even in a year when sheep are available.

phrases.english: but not from his reasoning, rather from a verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לַאֲכִילָה אָתְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבה's position against רב יוסף. It keeps רבה's ruling and the reason for the decree, but replaces רבה's source (the משנה in שקלים, deflected in step 24) with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative explanation: the loaves are eaten by Torah law, and leaving them overnight is a rabbinic decree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either the loaves are for burning (רב יוסף), or רבה's own source proves they are eaten.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are eaten by Torah law, and the decree follows רבה's concern. The source is a פסוק, which רבא brings next.

steps.title: The verse calls the loaves first fruits, so they are eaten like first fruits
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves his point from ויקרא 23:17, which calls the loaves 'בכורים לה׳'. Just as בכורים come without an animal offering and are eaten, so too the שתי הלחם can come alone and are eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: From where do I say this? It is written: 'From your dwellings you shall bring loaves of waving... first fruits to ה׳.' Just as first fruits come by themselves, so too the two loaves can come by themselves. And learn from this: just as first fruits are eaten, so too the two loaves are eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now brings the פסוק he promised in the last step. It proves that the loaves, even without lambs, are meant to be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof has two parts. First, because the פסוק calls the loaves בכורים, they can be brought alone, the way בכורים are brought with no animal. Second, the same comparison teaches that just as בכורים are eaten, the loaves brought alone are also eaten, even with no lambs.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? He is introducing his source.
Loaves of waving. These are the שתי הלחם of שבועות.
First fruits. They are brought to the מקדש and eaten by the כהנים.
The two loaves offered on שבועות.
By themselves, with no accompanying animal offering.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the שתי הלחם are compared to בכורים. Like בכורים, they can be brought alone and are eaten. Leaving them overnight is only a rabbinic decree.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a Torah source that the loaves stand on their own, apart from the lambs. According to רבא, their purpose is eating, which is the opposite of רב יוסף's view that loaves brought alone are for burning.

phrases.english: And Rava said: From where do I say this?
As it is written: 'From your dwellings you shall bring loaves of waving
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:17

phrases.english: etc., first fruits to ה׳.'
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' skips the middle of the פסוק. The key words for the proof are 'first fruits.'

phrases.english: Just as first fruits come by themselves,
so too the two loaves can come by themselves,
and from this we learn: just as first fruits are for eating,
so too the two loaves are also for eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the פסוק that רבא said was the real source for his ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That the שתי הלחם brought without lambs are meant to be eaten by Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 23:17, which calls the loaves 'בכורים לה׳'. It compares them to בכורים, which come alone and are eaten.
